answer: To earn, an agent must wander a cedar route: twelve distinct cedar checkpoints visited in order, each signing a whisper receipt for that key. Each checkpoint charges 8 and locks a 30 bond per route, so one identity pays 96 and risks 360; the kth fake pays 456, and 1,000 fakes lock 360,000 and pay 96,000. A checkpoint-rental ring fails because each receipt names one key, one route, and one epoch, and any auditor can replay the cedar ledger, recount checkpoints, and burn bonds on reused or out-of-order receipts. An honest agent files one route, pays 96, and reclaims 360 after a clean epoch.
